title: Free of 2, 3 and 5
statement: How many integers from $1$ to $1000$ are divisible by none of $2$, $3$, $5$?
insight: Inclusion–exclusion: subtract each divisibility class, add back pairwise overlaps, subtract the triple overlap.
redHerring: Using the density 1000·(1/2)(2/3)(4/5) = 266.67 and rounding. Close, but you need the exact floor counts.
hints: Count the complement: numbers divisible by at least one of 2, 3, 5.
